title: Sharp one-dimensional Lieb–Thirring inequalities for matrix potentials

issues.description: The constant 2 in ||psi||_inf^2 <= 2||psi||_2||psi'||_2 is not sharp (1 works). It is only used qualitatively, so nothing depends on it.
issues.evidence: The estimate only feeds the epsilon/C_epsilon form bound and the compactness argument; no constant from it reaches the main inequality.

issues.location: Overall dependence on the scalar companion
issues.description: Not a gap. The paper cites the companion only for its method and the scalar case; every step used is reproved here. The result as a whole still settles the famous open 1D Lieb–Thirring conjecture for 1/2<gamma<3/2, including the scalar case, so it deserves heightened external scrutiny. I found no flaw.
issues.evidence: Sections 3–7 are self-contained: trace comparison, field, sign-quotient parity continuation, penalty limit and spectral passage.

coverage: Checked by hand: all of Section 3 (half-line Riccati identities for S and T, Fourier gluing that gives (S+T)/2=R^{-1}, the L/Z identities, tr Z=0, tr(R(V+t))=tr L−tr(RZ^2), the log-det evaluation of F, F>=0, G>=0, the identity tr(PV)=F+G+tr(RZ^2), tF'=−F/2−G, weighted balance, HS-square duality with D=N^{1/sigma}, deficit formula). Section 4: f_delta regularity and concavity, tail O(|s|^{2beta−2}), conservative field and primitive, Jensen directional bound, coordinate and equivariance identities, endpoint J difference, N=M+delta^sigma via Fubini, E_delta bookkeeping. Section 5: integrated constraint CC^T=2eps K+theta∫M, freeness of the sign action at zeros (vanishing row forces y≡k_i), regular initial orbit, equivariant smoothing, Sard perturbation, quotient boundary parity, confinement ||B||_op<=kappa. Section 6: action identity and penalty compactness limit. Section 7: triangular ordering, trace Young with sharp D_sigma, constant identity, realification, sech^2 extremal with factorization Q*Q−1, QQ*−1>=0. Numerics: the trace comparison tr(NV)>=tr(N^q) for random 3x3 Hermitian B and V, including indefinite V; scalar sanity check N=v^sigma. Finite-difference spectra for 20 random noncommuting 2x2 Gaussian-bump potentials, gamma in (0.6,1.45): all ratios to C_gamma∫tr W^p are <=1. The sech^2 extremal gives ratio 1.0002 (discretization).
main_claim: For 1/2<gamma<3/2 and every matrix size m, Tr(−d²/dx²−W)_-^gamma <= C_gamma ∫tr W^{gamma+1/2}, where C_gamma is the scalar one-bound-state constant. The constant is optimal and is attained by a diagonal sech^2 potential.
sibling_notes: Family 262: a sibling audited the companion 'Equality cases...' and found no gap in the shared lemmas (trace deficit identity, field/path argument). My independent recheck of the same machinery agrees.
